author: Rachael Kauffman
title: Arrest warrant issued in Iowa City shooting that injured five people - NewsBreak
text:
By Rachael Kauffman No media credit provided. ,
1 hours ago
IOWA CITY, Iowa — Authorities announced during a press conference on Wednesday that an arrest warrant has been issued in the downtown Iowa City shooting that injured five people over the weekend.
On April 19, Iowa City Police officers were called to the 100 block of East College Street around 1:45 a.m. on reports of a large fight. As officers arrived on scene, gunfire was reported. Five victims were found, with one in critical condition and the four others stabilized. Three of the shooting victims were identified as University of Iowa students.
Story continues below
Later that same day, Iowa City police released images and requested information on five persons of interest in the investigation.
During a press conference on Wednesday, Iowa City Police Chief Liston shared further details leading up to and following the shooting. Chief Liston says at 1:45 a.m., a large fight broke out, reports show this fight involved around 40 people.
Chief Liston says 17-year-old Damarian M. Jones, of Cedar Rapids, was involved in the fight and stepped away for a moment during which he acquired a firearm from another individual and fired six shots into the crowd, injuring five people.
The Johnston County Attorney’s Office says Jones is wanted for an arrest warrant for five counts of Attempted Murder, three counts of Willful Injury Causing Serious Injury, two counts of Willful Injury Causing Bodily Injury, and Going Armed with Intent.
Photos courtesy of Iowa City Police. Authorities state Jones is believed to be number three. Three officers were on standard patrol in that area and were called to the scene just before the shots were fired, and arrived within minutes of the shooting. Authorities say officers provided first aid at the scene, including applying tourniquets, and one officer drove a victim to the hospital in their vehicle.
Chief Liston says at this time, three of the victims have been released from the hospital, while one remains hospitalized in stable condition and the other remains hospitalized in critical condition with a head injury.
Police say detectives arrived on the scene and began immediate efforts to gather evidence, including witness testimonies and video evidence from witnesses and businesses. Chief Liston says several persons of interest were identified on video, and more than three dozen search warrants have been carried out.
Law enforcement has recovered three firearms thus far and says the investigation remains ongoing, and more charges are likely to be filed in the case. Iowa City Police ask anyone with information to contact Detective Cade Burma at cburma@iowa-city.org or 319-356-5275. Tips can also be submitted anonymously using Crime Stoppers .
Reynolds, UI President, and others release statements following Iowa City shooting The University of Iowa Police says beginning immediately, their department will be assisting the city in downtown surveillance during weekends and busy days by providing four additional officers. Police say these measures will continue while law enforcement works on long-term security plans.
